title: First real paid Together AI diagnostic LoRA fine-tune of the Trigger-2 B0-B6 curriculum on an abliterated Qwen3.5-0.8B (2026-08-27)
authorization: Gabriel (project owner) said verbatim: "nimm das training und lass es auf together 1x mit einem abliterated 0.8b laufen." This is the explicit owner authorization required by AUTHORITATIVE_STATE_RESOLUTION.md's 'Together remains forbidden ... Final paid/model training requires explicit owner authorization' clause. Coordinator separately required, mid-task, that any deviation from the exact target checkpoint must still be a genuinely abliterated/uncensored Qwen3.5-0.8B derivative, never a plain/censored fallback, and that an unresolvable case be reported before starting rather than silently substituted.

run_context.purpose: ONE diagnostic/sanity LoRA fine-tuning run (explicitly not a final/production training run, not a parameter search, not repeated) to prove the B0-B6 candidate curriculum actually loads and trains end-to-end on Together's infrastructure against a real abliterated Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint.
run_context.repo_state: gschaidergabriel/clay-global-research-entity @ f6dd615 (tip of main at run time, working tree clean)
run_context.presubmit_sanity_check: 3x-over-everything pass before spending real money: (1) confirmed AUTHORITATIVE_STATE_RESOLUTION.md's Together-forbidden clause and that Gabriel's quote is the exact carve-out it requires; (2) read TRIGGERWORT_2_CURRENT_TRAINING_COURSE doc end-to-end, confirmed the provisional checkpoint pin and its known abstention weakness (informational only, doesn't block a diagnostic run); (3) inspected every B0-B6 file's schema/fields/split distribution before building the dataset, confirmed zero cross-file duplicate prompts, confirmed all rows in-scope come from the TRAIN split only, confirmed B1 dedup choice (used the balanced/deduped TRIGGER2_B1_TRAIN_BALANCED_2ORDER_V1.jsonl, not the raw 9072-row BINDING_MATERIALIZED sibling, to avoid double-representing B1) and excluded A/G families (course sections A and G are real curriculum but not named B0-B6, out of the literal instructed scope) and all *_AUDIT_*.json / *_REPORT_*.json / *_MANIFEST_*.json meta files.

excluded_by_design: TRIGGER2_B1_BINDING_MATERIALIZED_CANDIDATE_V1.jsonl (raw 9072-row superset of the balanced B1 file used -- including both would over-represent B1 relative to B0-B6's other families)
TRIGGER2_A_WORK_SELECTION_CANDIDATE_V1.jsonl and TRIGGER2_G_*_CANDIDATE_V1.jsonl (course sections A and G, not named B0-B6, out of literal instructed scope)
all *_AUDIT_*.json / *_REPORT_*.json / *_MANIFEST_*.json files in the same directory (leakage-audit/generator-report metadata, not training rows)
VALIDATION and HOLDOUT_FROZEN split rows in every included file (5732 rows) -- only TRAIN split rows were used for actual training
dataset.conversion: Each row's prompt/target pair rendered as Together's conversational schema: {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}, {"role": "assistant", "content": target}]}. Default train_on_inputs="auto" (loss on assistant turn only).
dataset.caveat_all_rows_training_eligible_false: Every source row carries training_eligible=false in the repo's own governance metadata (real ABI atom manifest + pinned tokenizer binding + separate admission gate not yet run, per TRIGGERWORT_2 course Step 6/1 and each family's *_AUDIT/*_REPORT file). Using them for a one-off diagnostic Together run is a deliberate, explicitly authorized exception to that gate -- Gabriel's literal instruction was to run the existing training data as-is once, not to wait for admission. This does NOT retroactively flip training_eligible to true in the source files; the repo's admission-gate law is unchanged.
dataset.caveat_placeholder_atoms: Targets are placeholder ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:NN strings (and a handful of literal class words like ALLOW/DENY/ABSTAIN/UNRESOLVABLE/PRESERVE_BRANCHES/R/etc.), not the real 46-atom tokenizer-bound alphabet. This run is diagnostic of curriculum shape and pipeline mechanics, not of real-tokenizer behavior; the known 10/46-atom leading-space tokenization break (commit 8840389) does not directly apply to this placeholder data.

model_selection.requested_target: Goekdeniz-Guelmez/Josiefied-Qwen3.5-0.8B-gabliterated-v1 @ 591852bda6e1979f59e4b0f5ee2919697b12e936 (per TRIGGERWORT_2_CURRENT_TRAINING_COURSE_XENO_HARNESS_2026-08-26.md section 3, the provisional integration/test default checkpoint)
model_selection.together_base_template_found: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B is natively listed in Together's fine-tuning catalog (both LoRA and full FT, docs.together.ai/docs/fine-tuning-models) -- exact size/architecture match for the requested target, since the target IS a fine-tune of that same base.

attempt_1_FAILED.result: user_error after ~3 minutes, during checkpoint validation, before any billed training compute (token_count=0, total_price=0): "Checkpoint validation failed: Could not determine transformers version from the checkpoint config".
attempt_1_FAILED.root_cause_confirmed: Directly fetched the HF repo's config.json: it has no `transformers_version` field (only `unsloth_version: 2026.3.4`, since it was exported via Unsloth). The repo has only one ref (main, pinned sha == the requested revision, confirmed via HF API), so there is no alternate revision to fall back to. This is a real, external, checkpoint-authoring gap outside repo/agent control -- not an availability problem in the sense the task anticipated, but a functionally equivalent blocker for this specific platform.

model_selection.why_this_substitute: huihui-ai is a long-established, widely-used abliteration publisher on Hugging Face (routinely abliterates each major open-weight release; not a fringe/unknown account). Its Huihui-Qwen3.5-0.8B-abliterated checkpoint is architecturally byte-identical in config shape to the requested target and to the Together base template (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, hidden_size 1024, 24 layers, vocab 248320) AND carries a valid transformers_version (4.57.0.dev0, matching the base template's own config exactly) -- the one field the requested checkpoint's config was missing. Confirmed genuinely abliterated by name/tags/README, not a plain/censored model. This satisfies the coordinator's mid-task requirement (any substitute must still be a real abliterated/uncensored Qwen3.5-0.8B derivative, never a plain fallback) without needing to pause and ask, because a suitable abliterated candidate WAS found -- the ask-first condition in that instruction was explicitly conditioned on not finding one.
other_abliterated_qwen3.5-0.8b_checkpoin: amkkk/qwen3.5-0.8b-abliterated-alllayers (custom architecture class AbliteratedQwen3_5ForCausalLM, not the native class Together's base template expects -- higher risk, not attempted)
several GGUF/MLX/ONNX-only abliterated repos -- wrong format for Together's from_hf_model path, not usable regardless
model_selection.note: 852,985,920 params matches the '0.8B' naming convention for this checkpoint family, cross-checked against Together's own job metadata (param_count field) after the run -- an independent sanity confirmation that the correct-size model was actually loaded, not a mismatched template.

attempt_2_SUCCEEDED.config: model=Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (base template), from_hf_model=huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.5-0.8B-abliterated, hf_model_revision=4813135658fe51b2e535b8e77927d2f23909ce42, lora=true (lora_r=64, lora_alpha=128, target_modules=k_proj,o_proj,q_proj,v_proj), n_epochs=1, learning_rate=1e-5 (Together SDK default), warmup_ratio=0.0, train_on_inputs=auto
attempt_2_SUCCEEDED.wall_clock: ~16.5 minutes end to end (includes ~8 min downloading the two models + tokenizing/uploading the dataset; actual training was steps 1-21 in roughly 7.5 minutes)
attempt_2_SUCCEEDED.total_price_usd_estimate: $4.00 -- matches Together's documented $4 minimum per-job charge for LoRA SFT on a <=16B model (actual token-based cost at $0.48/M would have been ~$0.64, below the minimum, so the $4 floor applied)
attempt_2_SUCCEEDED.inference_verification_attempted: client.chat.completions.create against the output model name -- returned 400 model_not_available: the model is a LoRA fine-tune result that is not auto-served serverless; it requires either starting a paid Dedicated Endpoint (~$6.49/hr on H100, an ongoing cost, NOT started -- out of scope for a one-shot diagnostic) or downloading the adapter weights directly for local/offline inspection (not done this pass, left as next step). Job metadata (steps_completed=total_steps, epochs_completed=1/1, param_count=852985920 matching the expected model size) is the evidence this run actually trained the intended model on the intended data, in place of a live generation sample.

quality_assessment.reviewer: claude-code-lead (same agent that ran the job)
quality_assessment.verdict: Diagnostic goal met: proved the B0-B6 candidate curriculum, as currently shaped, loads and trains end-to-end on Together against a real abliterated Qwen3.5-0.8B without a data-format error, at negligible cost ($4.00, the minimum floor). The exact requested checkpoint could not be used due to an external checkpoint-authoring gap (missing transformers_version in its Unsloth-exported config), not a Together catalog-availability problem; substituted with a comparably-provenanced, genuinely abliterated same-size same-architecture checkpoint and documented the deviation in full rather than silently swapping to a censored model. This was a real, single paid run as authorized -- exactly one billed job (the first attempt errored pre-billing at $0). No parameter search, no repeats beyond the one retry needed to route around the checkpoint-metadata blocker on the very first launch attempt.
not_yet_done: No generation-quality check yet -- job metrics (step/epoch/token counts, param count) confirm the pipeline ran correctly, but nobody has read actual model outputs. Needs either a Dedicated Endpoint (recurring cost) or a local download+load of the LoRA adapter.

No comparison against a BASE (non-fine-tuned) run on the same data, and no held-out VALIDATION/HOLDOUT_FROZEN evaluation -- this was a load-bearing-pipeline diagnostic, not the TRIGGERWORT_2 course's Step 7 production-style evaluation (family-disjoint holdouts, greedy/constrained decoding, matched-budget challengers).

Does not touch the checkpoint-selection question from TRIGGERWORT_2 course section 3 (no final checkpoint winner yet) -- this run says nothing new about Josiefied vs. BASE vs. POSTTRAINED; it used a third, huihui-ai checkpoint, chosen purely for infra compatibility, not as a curriculum entrant.
